title: Test speed: split the heavy Z bands of shared_face_bodies_finish into balanced sub-bands

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
`app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish` took 739 s in the release gate (`8643d9bb7`).
It is the longest step of the release gate.

We timed all six release bands in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` on 6 parallel workers (wall 891.67 s, sum 1,685.07 s):
- `band_6_of_6`: 891.66 s (52.9%)
- `band_4_of_6`: 755.60 s (44.8%)
- `band_5_of_6`: 21.72 s (1.3%)
- `band_3_of_6`: 6.53 s (0.4%)
- `band_1_of_6`: 5.43 s (0.3%)
- `band_2_of_6`: 4.13 s (0.2%)

Bands 4 and 6 take 1,647.26 s (97.8% of the binary).
Bands 1, 2, 3, and 5 finish in 37.81 s total (2.2%).
Even at `--test-threads=2`, Bands 4 and 6 already run at the same time.
Splitting this file into six binaries or sharding its six existing tests does not lower the 739 s floor.

What to do:
1. Replace the equal-height `BANDS = 6` split in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` with explicit Z-offset band edges.
2. Cut the Band 4 and Band 6 Z ranges into narrower sub-bands so no single band exceeds 150 s in release.
3. Update `the_3d_finish_bands_tile_the_whole_span` to verify gap-free coverage across all band edges from `top_of_model` to `bottom_of_model`.
4. Keep `the_3d_finish_band_split_levels_move_within_stepdown_and_links_cross_edge` and every gouge and `shank_hit` assertion unchanged.

Done means:
- Every heavy band test in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` finishes under 150 s in release.
- The bands tile the full 118 mm Z span with zero gaps.
- The `#[test]` count increases.
- Every test passes under `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test shared_face_bodies_finish -- --ignored`.

Part of #2556
